title: RO-MT086-ChildSessionRoleAssignment

scope.summary:
GOAL: Let an ORCHESTRATING SESSION assign roles to the workers it spawns: the spawn tool surface (MT-101) accepts an optional role_id (+ optional role_version), the role is resolved and injected at child spawn time via the MT-082 engine, a parent-child role attribution row records which role was assigned and by whom, and role assignment is constrained by the model-to-model policy (MT-106) — a parent may only assign roles its policy allows. This is the productized form of the repo-gov pattern where the orchestrator launches Coder/Validator sessions under their protocol prompts.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Spawn-request extension (role fields) through the MT-101 spawn tool surface into coordinator.rs spawn_session; role resolution + injection call in the spawn path; new SurrealKit rollout for the SCHEMAFULL role_assignments attribution table + typed store methods (in handshake_roles.rs or a sibling role_assignment.rs); policy check against the MT-106 model-to-model policy; typed errors + FR events; tests. Optional read route GET /api/sessions/{id}/role for attribution lookup.

DETAILED SPEC:
- Spawn surface: the MT-101 spawn tool schema gains { role_id?: string, role_version?: u32 }. Omitted = spawn without role (unchanged behavior). Version omitted = current ACTIVE version at spawn time, and the RESOLVED version is what gets recorded (never a floating reference).
- Resolution at spawn (coordinator.rs spawn_session seam): look up the role via HandshakeRoleStore; RoleNotFound / RoleNotActive -> typed spawn error BEFORE any process starts (fail-closed: no session spawns with a missing or unapproved role).
- Policy gate (MT-106): before injection, evaluate the parent's model-to-model policy: may this parent (its lane/model/own role) assign THIS role to a child? Deny -> typed RoleAssignmentDenied error + FR policy-denial event with { parent_session, requested_role, policy_rule }. The policy surface is MT-106's; this MT consumes its check API and adds the role-assignment predicate wiring.
- Injection: on allow, delegate to the MT-082 RoleInjectionEngine with the child's transport (claude/codex/acp); the child's spawn payload flows through the MT-083 composer when a task payload is present (composition consumes the same resolved role — one resolution, both consumers).
- Attribution records: SCHEMAFULL SurrealDB table role_assignments { assignment_id uuid, child_instance_id, role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, assigned_by_session, assigned_by_kind (operator|parent_model), policy_decision_ref, created_at } — answers 'which role, assigned by whom' for every role-carrying spawn. Operator-initiated launches (MT-085 picker) write the same rows with assigned_by_kind=operator, so attribution is uniform across operator and model spawns.
- Eventing: role_assigned FR event per successful spawn-with-role (joined to the MT-082 role_injected event via session id + sha256); role_assignment_denied on policy denial.
- Concurrency/attribution duties (HBR-SWARM): attribution rows are written in the same transaction scope as the spawn registration so a crash between spawn and attribution cannot yield an attributed-less role session; parallel spawns by multiple parents must not interleave attribution rows incorrectly (per-child uniqueness: one role assignment per child instance).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-101 spawn tool surface contract and coordinator.rs spawn_session (verified seam: pub async fn spawn_session(&self, mut request: SpawnRequest)) to place the role fields and resolution hook.
2. Extend SpawnRequest + the MT-101 tool schema with optional role_id/role_version; thread through operator_chat.rs build_spawn_request so the MT-085 picker path reuses the same fields.
3. Implement spawn-time resolution with fail-closed typed errors (RoleNotFound/RoleNotActive) before process start.
4. Wire the MT-106 policy check with the role-assignment predicate; implement RoleAssignmentDenied + denial FR event.
5. Add the role_assignments definition to the MT-332 SurrealKit rollout + typed store methods (insert within the same SurrealDB transaction as spawn registration; get_by_child; list_by_parent).
6. Call the MT-082 injection engine on allow; pass the resolved role to the MT-083 composer when composing a task payload (single resolution object shared).
7. Wire role_assigned FR event.
8. Optional GET /api/sessions/{id}/role read route over the attribution store.
9. Tests: spawn-with-role happy path (attribution row + both FR events, resolved version pinned); spawn-without-role unchanged; RoleNotActive fail-closed (no process spawned — assert via stub spawner); policy-deny path (typed error + denial event + no injection + no attribution row); version-resolution test (omitted version records the then-active version); parallel-spawn attribution test (two parents, two children, rows attributed correctly, one-assignment-per-child enforced).
forbidden_paths: app/src/** except named IPC read surfaces
.GOV/** (role protocols are read-only source material; importer reads, never writes)
acceptance_criteria: MT-101 spawn tool surface accepts optional role_id/role_version; omitting them preserves existing spawn behavior byte-for-byte.
Spawn with a missing, draft, or retired role fails closed with a typed error before any child process starts.
Parent policy (MT-106) gates every model-initiated role assignment; denial yields RoleAssignmentDenied, a denial FR event, no injection, and no attribution row.

Successful role-carrying spawns produce exactly one role_assignments row per child with resolved role_version, overlay_sha256, assigned_by_session, and assigned_by_kind; operator-picker launches write the same rows with assigned_by_kind=operator.
Attribution row insertion shares the spawn-registration transaction scope; a simulated failure between spawn and attribution leaves no role-injected-but-unattributed session.
role_assigned FR events join to MT-082 role_injected events via session id + overlay_sha256.
Omitted role_version resolves and RECORDS the active version at spawn time (no floating references in attribution).
Parallel spawns from two parents attribute correctly under concurrency (test-proven); one role assignment per child instance is uniqueness-enforced.
UserManual documents the spawn role_id surface and attribution lookup in the same change.
expected_tests: fail-closed not-active/not-found tests (stub spawner asserts no process)
policy-deny test (no injection, no row, denial event)
parallel two-parent attribution + per-child uniqueness test
implementation_notes: Verified seam: coordinator.rs line ~548 pub async fn spawn_session(&self, mut request: SpawnRequest) -> SwarmResult<ModelInstanceId>; operator_chat.rs OperatorChatLaunchService::build_spawn_request is the operator-path producer of SpawnRequest — extend the request type once, both paths inherit.

One resolution, two consumers: resolve the role once per spawn and hand the same resolved object to injection (MT-082) and composition (MT-083); never resolve twice (version could change between resolutions).

MT-106 owns policy semantics; this MT only adds the role-assignment predicate call and the deny plumbing. If MT-106's check API lacks a role predicate, raise the seam gap to the packet rather than inventing local policy.

Repo-gov precedent being productized: orchestrator launches Coder/WP Validator sessions under role protocols with attributable session ids — role_assignments is the typed successor of that session-registry attribution.
Attribution rows are audit data: no delete route; retire/cleanup follows the session-lifecycle retention policy, not role lifecycle.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend spawn/policy/attribution MT; the operator-visible picker is MT-085 and attribution surfaces via the read route + FR events (trace projection).

target_entries: spawn-role-assignment: role_id/role_version spawn fields, fail-closed rules (active-only), parent policy gating, attribution lookup (GET /api/sessions/{id}/role), failure/recovery (RoleNotActive, RoleAssignmentDenied)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.behavior: role-carrying child spawn (resolution, policy gate, injection, attribution)
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1; role_assigned/role_assignment_denied FR events + attribution rows are the Tier-1 evidence surface.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.behavior: policy denial of a model-initiated role assignment
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Denials must be first-class evidence (who asked for what and which rule refused), not silent fallbacks; same Tier-2/3 deferral as above.

risk_if_missed: Orchestrating sessions cannot delegate under roles: child workers spawn roleless (unsteered) or parents smuggle role text through ad-hoc prompts with no policy gate, no attribution, and no audit joins — the multi-agent steering premise of WP-017 fails at its main consumption point.

risks: RISK-1: Privilege escalation via roles — a constrained parent assigns a child a powerful role (e.g. broad tool allow-list), laundering capabilities the parent itself was denied.
RISK-2: Unattributed role sessions — a crash or non-transactional write between injection and attribution leaves a running session whose role nobody can prove afterward.
RISK-3: Floating version resolution — recording 'current' instead of the resolved version means later activations silently rewrite what history claims was injected.
RISK-4: Fail-open on registry outage — if the role lookup errors and the spawn proceeds roleless (or worse, with a cached overlay), the operator believes a role ran that did not.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): MT-106 policy check runs on every model-initiated assignment with the parent's own identity/role as input; deny is typed + evented; test includes an escalation fixture (parent denied a role it requests for a child).
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): attribution insert shares the spawn-registration transaction; failure-injection test proves no injected-but-unattributed session can exist.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): resolution pins and records the concrete version + overlay_sha256 in the attribution row; test asserts recorded version survives a subsequent activate of a newer version.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): registry lookup errors abort the spawn with a typed error (fail-closed); no cached-overlay path exists; stub-spawner test asserts zero processes on lookup failure.

research_provenance.source: Inspected coordinator.rs spawn_session and operator_chat.rs OperatorChatLaunchService::build_spawn_request/launch as the two SpawnRequest producers; MT-101 spawn tool surface and MT-106 model-to-model policy as declared cross-family seams; MT-082 injection + MT-083 composition as consumers of one resolution; repo-gov precedent: orchestrator-managed role session launches with session-registry attribution (.GOV/roles/orchestrator protocol + session-control scripts).
corrections: Fail-closed everywhere: no role-carrying spawn proceeds on lookup error, non-active status, or policy denial.
Attribution is uniform: operator-picker launches and model-initiated spawns write the same role_assignments rows, differing only in assigned_by_kind.
Versions are pinned at resolution time; attribution never stores floating 'current' references.

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.schema_rule: The role_assignments entity and uniqueness/transaction invariants are implemented as SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL through SurrealKit, never as SQL up/down migrations.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.proof_rule: All persistence, transaction, restart, concurrency, and privacy proofs run against real Handshake-managed SurrealDB with authenticated record users.
